rationale.headline: Brazil is the clear favourite (81%) — its passing play is the harder one to break down.

drivers.label: Passing structure
drivers.detail: Brazil spreads passes across more players and fewer go through one pivot, so it keeps more routes forward when pressed. (Passing-network detail was unavailable, so this leans on possession and pressing instead.)

drivers.label: Ball control
drivers.detail: Brazil keeps the ball more (49% vs 48%), dictating the tempo of build-up.

drivers.label: Scoring threat
drivers.detail: Brazil has created the better chances on average (1.94 vs 1.39 expected goals a game).

rationale.methodNote: Market-blind: three one-vs-rest random forests (60 CART trees each, depth 5, 70% feature subsampling) over the A-minus-B difference of passing-network graph features (density, centralization, top-5 edge share) and style features (possession, high-press share, expected-goal rate); forest scores are clamped to [0,1] and normalised to a 1X2 distribution. Training rows are leakage-safe (each rebuilt from matches strictly before its date) and fall back to a logistic model on structure and attack gaps under eight rows. No betting or market data was used.
